gen-dafont-college-gf-esteban: College is dynamic and authoritative, every curve matching the weight of its straight stems, while Esteban keeps its thin parts barely slimmer. Solid weight everywhere, with a refined, classic lowercase that looks oversized.
gen-dafont-college-gf-faustina: Authoritative from the first stroke, College keeps a constant line from top to baseline, with no thinning at curves. Faustina tightens its stroke slightly at curve tops and has an open-jawed c, like pliers.
gen-dafont-college-gf-halant: College has no hairlines to squint at, every curve built as sturdy as its straight stems. Halant adds a faint, friendly thick-thin shift and outward-pointing terminals, and the whole pairing feels authoritative.
gen-dafont-college-gf-hedvig-letters-ser: Confident, with not a calligraphic swell anywhere. College does best at plain, dynamic outlines, while Hedvig Letters Serif does best at mild, letterpress-slug thick-thin variation and sturdy lowercase.
gen-dafont-college-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa spills its counters into the surrounding space and makes words look sturdy and large. College sits beside it with diagonals matching its stems, so the two feel dynamic and editorial together.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-ovo: Ovo reads with a soft-pencil gentleness, its thins barely lighter than its thicks and its curve terminals spaciously open. Conthrax stays geometric above, and Ovo paragraphs would glide like one thread.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-faustina: Faustina brings classic, authoritative bowls that thin gracefully. Disorder does best at raw, constant-width pen lines and widely spaced glyphs, while Faustina does best at medium-key contrast and an open-jawed c.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-hedvig-letters-se: Chaotic and raw, Disorder joins strokes without thinning where curves meet stems. Hedvig Letters Serif steps in with mild, friendly contrast and open-ended curves that have room to breathe.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa reads sturdy and large, its counters spilling into the surrounding space and its contrast flexed like spring wire. Below Disorder's raw, spread-out glyphs, paragraphs would feel steady and approachable.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-montagu-slab: Disorder sketches raw, chaotic letters with a pencil-line consistency. Montagu Slab follows with robust downstrokes, slender turns and a sizable x-height, so a page of it would read in a refined, traditional way.
